programme.desc: Tha na planntraisean 's na lusan aig Mamaidh ri cleòcadh san teas ach, gu fortanach, tha deagh bheachd aig Meanbh airson Mamaidh a chuideachadh len uisgeachadh. Mother’s plants and flowers are wilting in the heat but fortunately, Tiny has a brilliant idea to help Mother out with watering.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha tòrr a’ gabhail àite an-diugh is tha Meanbh is Beag a’ faighinn dìoghladh ’son bhith foighidneach is grad-smuainteach an-diugh. Much is happening today, and Tiny and Small are getting rewarded for their patience and quick thinking.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona air bhioran! Tha i air cluinntinn g' eil gealach fìor shònraichte gu bhith ann a-nochd - sàr-ghealach. Ag ràdh ris a h-uile duine gum feum iad fuireach air an cois son a faicinn, an tig aice fhèin air fuireach na dùisg air a shon? Oona is a very excited puffin! She has heard that there is to be a very special moon tonight - a super-moon. Telling everyone that they must stay up to see it, will she be able to stay awake herself?

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Baba a' lorg slige dheàrrsach a tha e airson a thoirt dhachaigh. Ge-tà, 's ann a tha rudan deàrrsach cuideachad a còrdadh ri faoileagan a tha airson an t-slige fhaighinn dhaibh p-fhèin! An tèid aig Oona 's Baba air teicheadh dhachaigh bhuapa? Baba finds a shiny shell that he wants to keep and take home with him. However, the seagulls also love shiny objects and want the shell for themselves! Will Oona and Baba be able to escape them and get home safely?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing air fhàgail cuide ri Sula 's Amma fhad 's a tha Flop sa bhùth a ceannachd biadh son lòn. Ge-tà, chan eil fad ann gus eil Bing ag ionndrainn Flop gu mòr! Bing finds himself being left with Sula and Amma when Flop goes to the shop to buy some food for lunch. However, it doesn't take Bing long to realise how much he misses Flop!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing 's Pando air an aon bhogsa-lòin ùr fhaighinn, fear gleansach Hoppity Voosh! Ged 's e spòrs a th' ann an aon bhogsa bhith aca, tha beagan ùpraid ag èirigh nuair a thig am biadh aca am measg a chèile! Bing and Pando have the same lunchbox - a shiny new Hoppity Voosh one! Although it's fun to have the same box, the friends soon realise that it can cause great confusion when their lunches are mixed up!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha pàrantan Raghnaill air falbh air chuairt, is tha iad a’ fàgail “Antaidh as fheàrr”, piuthar òg màthair Raghnaill os cionn chùisean. Tha Antaidh coma mu riaghailtean is mu dheireadh thall, tha a’ chlann a’ faicinn cò ris a tha dachaigh gun riaghailtean coltach, fiù ’s Raghnall! Roman's parents are travelling, and they leave 'our favourite aunt', the young and laid-back Roman's mom's sister, in charge. The kids finally experience a house without rules, even Roman!

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha na Pluic an dùil a dhol sìos chun na tràghad airson co-là-breith Anna, ach nuair a tha biadh partaidh Phòil gan dèanamh beag bìodach, feumaidh iad dòigh eile a lorg airson faighinn ann. The Spuds have planned a trip to the seaside for Anna’s birthday, but when Dave’s party food shrinks them, they must adapt and find a way for the outing to still go ahead.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Granaidh air a bualadh le dealanach, is tha seo ga fàgail làn dealain. Feumaidh Pòl feuchainn ris an dealain aice a dhrùdhadh aiste coltach ri bataraidh, mus dèan i cus cron. When Gran gets struck by lightning and charged with electrical powers, Dave must run her down like a battery before she causes too much mischief.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Air an slighe gu Fèill Geamhraidh Throlberg, tha Hilda, Flòraidh is Daibhidh a’ tighinn tarsainn air daoine beaga èibhinn, a tha a’ lorg clann a tha rasgach. Ach carson? On their way to the Trolberg Winter Festival, Hilda, Flòraidh and Daibhidh come across funny little characters, who are looking for naughty children. But why?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Latha trang eile aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche le Ciorstaidh an Loiliopop a’ lìbhrigeadh Là Sàbhailteachd Rathaid agus Danny an Janny trang le Là Sàbhailteachd Teine. Bidh na camarathan againne a’ leantainn a h-uile rud a thachras tron latha. A hectic day at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche with Ciorstaidh overseeing Road Safety Day, while Danny is also busy with Fire Safety Day. Our cameras follow all the events of this important day in the school calendar.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach seachdainn le sgioba-naidheachd BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Iain MacKinnon reads excerpts from Gliocas bhon Bhioball by Donald Saunders, and Mairi MacInnes narrates from The Mother’s Catechism.

programme.title: Dealbhan Fraoich/Heather's Portraits
programme.desc: Combining the role of artist and interviewer, Heather Dewar creates colour portraits of well-known Gaels, while teasing out of them every little detail of their life story! Heather meets Ciorstag Wilson, who recently moved back to her native Mull after spending years on the mainland. Not only is Ciorstag a teacher in Tobermory, but she is one of Gaeldom’s most celebrated social media influencers, posting video tutorials and tips on make-up and beauty. Tha Fraoch Nic an Deòir a Ìle air ais air an sgrion le sreath ùr de “Dhealbhan Fraoich”. An dà chuid na tè-ealain agus na ceasnaiche, tha i a’dèanamh dealbhan dathte de Ghàidheil air a bheil sinn eòlach – agus a’tàladh asta iomadh sgeul mu eachdraidh am beatha. Sa chiad phrògram dhen t-sreath tha Fraoch a’coinneachadh ri Ciorstag NicUilleim, a thill dhachaigh a Mhuile o chionn ghoirid, as dèidh bliadhnaichean air tìr-mòr. Chan e mhàin gu bheil Ciorstag a’teagasg – ach tha i ainmeil air Ghaidhealtachd mar thè le buaidh air na meadhanan shòisealta, a’cur leasain bhideo air-loidhne, is molaidhean mu mhaise gnùis agus bòidhchead. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Suas gu Deas
programme.desc: Se latha geamaichean Uibhist a Deas a th’ann agus tha farpais iasgaich ann am Barraigh. A fishing competition is held in Barra, while Highland dancers compete at the South Uist games.

programme.title: An Cogadh Fuar: Cold War Stories
programme.desc: Stories of how the Cold War impacted the lives of ordinary people. Sgeulachdan mu mar a thug an Cogadh Fuar buaidh air beatha dhaoine àbhaisteach.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le The Poozies le Wired to the Moon agus Sausage. Clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads 2025 ann an Obar Dheathain. Concert set performed by The Poozies, featuring the tracks Wired to the Moon and Sausage. Originally recorded live at the 2025 Trad Awards in Aberdeen.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Ceòl dùthchasach agus traidiseanta air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. Chaidh Seirm Celtic Connections a’ chlàradh ann an 2022 agus tha an ceathramh prògram seo a’ foillseachadh iomadachd na fèise tro thaisbeanaidhean le Leyla McCalla, Dlù, Stundom, Norman Blake, James Grant and Monica Queen. Traditional music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Seirm Celtic Connections was filmed in 2022 and this episode reflects the diversity of the festival. With appearances by Leyla McCalla, Dlù, Stundom, plus Norman Blake, James Grant and Monica Queen.

programme.title: Luchd-Brathaidh Cogaidh | Spies of War
programme.desc: 1962: Tha an saoghal air fad air bhioran agus cogadh niùclasach air fàire ri linn astasan Sobhietach ann an Cùba. Air cùl ghnothaichean, tha neach-brathaidh Sobhietach a’ cuideachadh Kennedy an aghaidh Khruschev. Ionnsaich mar a bhrath Oleg Penkovsky an t-Aonadh Sobhietach – agus mar a chaidh an Treas Cogadh Saoghail a sheachnadh. 1962: The world holds its breath as nuclear war looms during the Cuban Missile Crisis. Behind the scenes, a Soviet spy helps Kennedy face Khrushchev. Discover how Oleg Penkovsky betrayed the USSR - and helped avert World War III. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: The first ever episode of the landmark natural history series Life on Earth. David Attenborough explores the wildlife and landscape that inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution.

programme.title: Afoot Again in the Past
programme.desc: Esther Rantzen finds peace and tranquillity at Salisbury Cathedral, Jack Charlton visits Warkworth Castle in Northumberland and Dora Bryan celebrates the beauty of ballrooms.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Timeshift journeys back to a lost era of rail travel, when trains had names, character and style. Once the pride of the railway companies that ran them, the named train is now largely consigned to railway history. Writer and presenter Andrew Martin asks why we once named trains and why we don't do so any more. He embarks on three railway journeys around Britain, following the routes of three of the most famous named trains - the Flying Scotsman, the Cornish Riviera Express and the Brighton Belle. We reflect on travel during the golden age of railways - when the journey itself was as important as reaching your destination - and compare those same journeys with the passenger experience today.

programme.title: Michael Palin's Hemingway Adventure
programme.desc: Michael Palin continues to trace Hemingway's journey. He arrives in Key West in time for Hemingway's 100th birthday celebrations, where he is given boxing lessons from 83-year-old Shine Forbes, who sparred with Hemingway. In Uganda, Michael has his hair cut en route up the Nile. At Butiaba, Uganda he visits the site of a plane crash Hemingway was involved in. Finally, Michael reaches Venice in time for the carnival and then tries his hand at duck-hunting in nearby Caorle.

programme.title: Michael Palin's Hemingway Adventure
programme.desc: Michael Palin stays in Ernest Hemingway's favourite Cuban hotel and samples a few of his favourite hangouts, including Bodeguita del Medio and the Floridita in old Havana. He meets 101-year-old Gregorio Fuentes, considered an Old Man of the Sea, and who sits in the sun, smoking cigars. He peers into Hemingway's Havana house that has now become a shrine where visitors aren't allowed to tread. Back in West America, Michael attempts to be a cowboy and partakes in some male bonding while visiting Yellowstone Park. He also visits the house in Ketchum, Idaho, where Hemingway died in 1961 and where he was laid to rest.

programme.title: Five to Eleven
programme.desc: Emma Thompson reads poetry and prose.

programme.title: Sondheim at the BBC
programme.desc: A celebration of the work of one of the great songwriters and lyricists, Stephen Sondheim, who passed away in November 2021 at the age of 91. A giant of musical theatre, Sondheim first found international fame in 1957 as the lyricist for Leonard Bernstein’s West Side Story and would inspire generations from that moment on. This selection includes some of Sondheim’s finest songs, broadcast on the BBC over a period of 60 years, with performances from a cast of his friends and fans that features some of the biggest names of stage and screen, including Shirley Bassey, Sammy Davis Jr, Michael Ball and Liza Minnelli.

programme.title: Britain's Most Fragile Treasure
programme.desc: Dr Janina Ramirez unlocks the secrets of a centuries-old masterpiece in glass, the Great East Window at York Minster, the largest expanse of medieval stained glass in the UK.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: One of the fastest growing sectors in tourism, both in the UK and globally, is being driven by people visiting locations that have been featured in films. In a special edition Talking Movies investigates the booming film tourism business also known as 'set jetting'. In London, Tom Brook joins a James Bond walking tour visiting key locations used in 007 films and talks to people helping to attract visitors through the capital's cinematic history. In Austria, the 1965 classic The Sound of Music brings in an estimated 300,000 visitors each year. Tom joins a group of fans who burst into spontaneous renditions of the musical's beloved songs as they travel through Salzburg's streets. The Oscar-winning picture Anora set in and around Brighton Beach in New York has resulted in a whole new wave of tourists visiting this Russian speaking community. We see some key locations used in the movie and hear from the picture's celebrated director Sean Baker on why he wanted to shoot there. And Tom visits the French town of Dinard which capitalises on movie tourism through its annual film festival in Northern France.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: This week John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, examines the new deal aimed at ending the war between the US and Iran, analyses Ukraine's bid to join the European Union and looks at the worsening situation for women in Afghanistan under Taliban rule.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Giving birth in the UK is getting more dangerous; the number of women dying in childbirth is up 20% in the last ten years. Now, in Nottingham, the largest-ever maternity inquiry is underway, reviewing the medical records of thousands of births for signs of avoidable harm. Reporting for Panorama, Michael Buchanan hears powerful testimonies: from mothers who weren’t listened to, staff who blew the whistle but were ignored, and from parents whose babies’ tragic deaths were dismissed as ‘just bad luck’. The programme also hears from the new chief executive of the Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, who has promised change. As families unite to demand answers, Panorama investigates how systemic neglect, inadequate staffing and a reluctance to learn from mistakes have led to heartbreak.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Young people were told artificial intelligence would make them sharper, faster, more creative - and more employable. But for many, that promise now feels more complicated. From students leaning on chatbots to write essays to graduates sending out hundreds of AI-assisted job applications - only to be filtered out by algorithms on the other side - artificial intelligence is no longer a future story. Join AI Decoded as we ask: Is AI empowering the next generation - or quietly undermining it?

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: Across the world, fashion is a fundamental expression of who we are. Today, people in China are rediscovering the beauty of their extraordinarily rich clothing heritage. In this programme, Alastair discovers how historic fashion design still resonates with people in China today, and how it has become a way in which people can celebrate their identity.

programme.title: The President's Path
programme.desc: Caitríona Perry is joined by White House reporter Bernd Buzman and CBS News political director Fin Gomez to unpack the memorandum of understanding with Iran, signed with a flourish by President Trump before G7 leaders at Versailles. With a 60-day clock now running toward bigger talks, they ask what America has actually gained - given the Strait of Hormuz was open and petrol cheaper before Operation Epic Fury began. The team digs into the unresolved nuclear question, the daunting task of diluting Iran's enriched uranium on a timeline that took the Obama administration 20 months, and the politics driving it all: JD Vance positioning himself as the face of the deal, midterm pressures and an uneasy MAGA base. They also weigh a renewed push on Ukraine, rumours swirling around Cuba, and a strikingly public rift between Trump and Netanyahu. Could the flashpoint in Lebanon yet unravel the whole Iran deal?

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Following the sentencing of 13 people for violent disorder during protests in Southampton, attention has turned to the role of content creators who film demonstrations and public disorder. The judge cited the usefulness of footage filmed by so-called 'citizen journalists'. Siddharth Venkataramakrishnan of the Institute for Strategic Dialogue and content creator Wesley Winter give their perspective on the issue. The BBC has begun setting out changes as part of plans to deliver significant savings across the organisation. The measures include the closure of several programmes across radio and current affairs output, alongside wider reductions in staffing. Jonathan Munro, global director of BBC News, outlines the changes. Norma Percy has spent years getting to the heart of some of the biggest moments in recent history. Her documentaries have been celebrated for talking directly to the people who made the decisions. As the BBC airs her latest film - about Brexit - she reflects on her storied career and the future of documentary-making.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Tunisia play their second game in Group F against Japan at Monterrey Stadium. Tunisia’s shock group-stage win against France in Qatar in 2022 was only their third victory across six World Cup appearances. This is their third successive appearance at the tournament. Japan made their World Cup debut in 1998 and alternated between getting knocked out in the group stage and reaching the round of 16 in their first six appearances. They broke the cycle four years ago by making the knockout stage for the second time in a row. Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma and Daizen Maeda of Celtic could play key roles.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as Spain play their second game in Group H against Saudi Arabia at the Atlanta Stadium. As the reigning European champions, Spain will be favourites to win Group H, but they struggled at the last World Cup, losing in the group stages against Japan and being knocked out at the Round of 16 by Morocco. Saudi Arabia secured one of the greatest ever World Cup giant-killings four years ago when they beat eventual champions Argentina. The only time they have reached the knockout stages came when the tournament was last held in the US in 1994.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Away from Hampshire's famous ports and bustling harbours lies a wild world of woodland, heathland and chalk streams. Matt Baker and Charlotte Smith meet the people working to find, protect and celebrate the county's lesser-spotted wildlife. Charlotte also investigates how proposed changes to visa rules could affect sheep shearing in the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow travels to beautiful Beaumaris Castle on the island of Anglesey, north Wales, where presenter Fiona Bruce learns about the history and heritage of the Menai Bridge. Treasures discovered by our team of experts include a dog collar from 1765, a Royal Doulton vase with a dragon decoration and an atlas of Anglesey. Joanna Hardy is thrilled to find jewellery once owned by Lady Megan Lloyd George, daughter of David Lloyd George, the former prime minister. She was the first female MP for Wales and represented Anglesey. Lisa Lloyd spots an articulated Saba doll made in the 1920s, and watch-and-clock specialist Ben Wright values a large pocket watch, also known as a coach watch. Heading north from Anglesey lies the Isle of Man, where Marc Allum finds a collection of trophies from the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy (TT) road racing event for motorcycles. And Fiona’s observational skills are put to the test by Asian art specialist Alexandra Aguilar, who presents three objects that may not be all they first seem.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Live coverage as World Cup debutants Cape Verde play their second match in Group H, taking on former winners Uruguay in Miami. Cape Verde, a group of islands in the Atlantic Ocean with a population of just over 500,000, finished top of their qualifying group, beating Cameroon along the way. The Blue Sharks have twice reached the quarter-finals of the Africa Cup of Nations. Uruguay, winners of the inaugural tournament in 1930, are managed by former Leeds manager Marcelo Bielsa and qualified for a fourth consecutive World Cup, beating Brazil and Argentina in the process. They are captained by Real Madrid’s Federico Valverde.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026

Tunisia’s shock group-stage win against France in Qatar in 2022 was only their third victory across six World Cup appearances. This is their third successive appearance at the tournament. Japan made their World Cup debut in 1998 and alternated between getting knocked out in the group stage and reaching the round of 16 in their first six appearances. programme.title: Funboys
programme.desc: As Callum begins slowly unravelling under the strain of Jordan's relentless night terrors about baldness, he stumbles upon a flyer for Ballymacbot Wars - a local robot combat tournament offering a generous cash prize and potential ticket out of Jordan’s bedroom. Meanwhile, Jordan is uncharacteristically uninterested in the whole affair. He's become a bald hermit, terrified to leave the house and expose his creamy scalp to the outside world. That is, until, like a dagger in the night, a hooded burst of inspiration sends him back out into the world… and the robot wars.

programme.title: PRU
programme.desc: It’s Sienna’s first day at the PRU and a chance for a fresh start. She makes a new friend in troubled Belle, reunites with frosty old schoolmate Jaeden and crosses swords with hyperactive Halil, who is refusing to take his ADHD medication. When Halil’s behaviour threatens the class paintballing trip, Sienna takes matters into her own hands, with disastrous consequences.

programme.title: PRU
programme.desc: The kids are introduced to the ‘power of manifestation’ by holier-than-thou life coach Noah. However, Sienna takes a dislike to him and leads a rebellion. Meanwhile, Belle contemplates sending a nude, Jaeden struggles with home responsibilities, and Halil is left shocked as his manifestations appear to come true.

programme.title: PRU
programme.desc: Romance is in the air as Jean and Anthony take the kids camping in the woods. The kids struggle to navigate the area, the elements and, ultimately, each other. They have to plant the flag before sundown, but an emergency arises when Belle goes missing. Meanwhile, the teachers get carried away and have a few too many, while Jaeden’s arachnophobia threatens to get the better of him.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: The Doctor and Clara face their last Christmas. Trapped on an Arctic base, under attack from terrifying creatures, who are you going to call? Santa Claus!

programme.title: OnlyFans: Inside the Machine
programme.desc: Behind the billion-pound success of OnlyFans lies a hidden ecosystem of exploitation. A BBC Current Affairs investigation uncovers allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed by some of the hundreds of agents who manage many of the platform’s creators as well as the potential for modern slavery. Through survivor testimony, undercover access to a managers’ chat forum and expert legal analysis, the film exposes an industry where young women are trapped, threatened and profited from - raising urgent questions about accountability at the heart of one of Britain's most lucrative tech companies.

programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Vick Hope are in the Cotswolds, exploring one of Britain’s most iconic rural landscapes. While its rolling countryside, historic villages and farming heritage attract visitors from far and wide, protecting what makes the region special is an ongoing challenge. John meets the people helping to support nature and sustainable farming, while Vick discovers the skills and craftsmanship preserving the distinctive character of the Cotswolds. Meanwhile, Adam Henson gets hands-on with some of the region’s rare breeds and the efforts to secure their future.

programme.title: Capability Brown's Unfinished Garden
programme.desc: Capability Brown is known as the founder of landscape design. In the 1700s, he created some of the most magnificent landscapes in England. He travelled the length and breadth of the country, improving more than 200 of the greatest estates in the land for some of the most influential people of the 18th century. But there is one plan that never got off the drawing board. The only land Capability ever owned was in Fenstanton, Cambridgeshire, but he died before he could carry out any plans for his own garden. Today, it is a piece of flat land bisected by the A14 dual carriageway. Landscape designer and Gardeners' Question Time regular Bunny Guinness travels across England to some of Capability's finest landscapes - Blenheim, Burghley, Milton Abbey and Castle Ashby - to understand what he might have created. Rediscovering plans and letters, and using the latest technology, Capability Brown's unfinished garden is brought to life.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Beechgrove Garden is full of information for gardeners across the country who have to cope with the colder climates of the UK. Beechgrove has had some cold nights even recently, but now it looks like it’s safe to plant out those tender varieties, so Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham are finally putting in the ground varieties that wouldn't survive a frost. In a warmer environment, Lizzie is checking on her tomatoes, and this year she is comparing hybrid and heritage varieties, with both needing some attention right now to maximise their productivity. Brian is in the Accessible Garden looking at recent changes that will make the plot easier to move around and work in for anyone with mobility problems. There is also a trip to Leven to catch up with Calum in his allotment, and there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads to Montrose beach to measure the increasing rate of coastal erosion. Rosie is near Edinburgh meeting the farming brothers who regenerated their business into a top foodie destination. Shahbaz is in St Andrews finding out about the artists who accurately captured changes in our coastline before cameras were invented. Leanna visits Huntly to find out why it’s the perfect location for swifts. And as the annual clip gets underway, Cammy gives apprentice Anne a masterclass in the art of shearing.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt shares a delicious tasting menu from Saturday Kitchen chefs. Maria Elia serves up pulled duck burgers with an apple, peach and ouzo slaw and duck fat popcorn. Tony Singh rustles up langoustine en papillote with a honey, lime and ginger dressing, blanched asparagus and Jersey Royals on the side. To celebrate Britain’s love of a picnic, Matt has three variants on sausage rolls, from simple herbs to Mexican spices. Mandy Yin brings her Malaysian chicken curry and flaky flatbreads, while Julius Roberts cooks his courgette cavatelli. Olly Smith touts the virtues of chardonnay, and Paloma Faith tucks into either her food heaven, Spanish fish stew, or her food hell, beetroot pithivier. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes fishing for bass in Jersey, and the Hairy Bikers explore the fragrant benefits of bergamot.

programme.title: Mary Berry - Cook and Share
programme.desc: Mary bowls the England players over at Edgbaston with her cricket tea, steps onto the crease for a quick coaching session and shares more of her mouthwatering recipes.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Former Mr Gay Wales Paul Davies calls on Andi’s help to make Merthyr Tydfil’s first ever Pride a roaring success. While Prides have been popping up in the Welsh Valleys in recent years, this is set to be their biggest yet, but first there are two problems Andi needs to solve – food and transport. Andi sets about creating a true Valleys Pride flamboyant feast that uses local produce and draws on tradition while also celebrating difference. Then, in a bid to bring as many revellers as possible to this historic event, she hires a bus and tries to fill it with as many locals as possible, while also delving into the historic bond between miners and the gay and lesbian community, which dates back to the 1980s. With the Welsh weather threatening to make the whole event a washout, can Andi still bring the joy she’s promised Paul and make Merthyr’s inaugural Pride truly momentous?

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater raids his cupboards, fridge and vegetable patch to create a week's worth of delicious meals. In this edition, he demonstrates how to make our ingredients go just that little bit further. Whether it's adding grated beetroot to make a tasty meatball supper feed the masses, or putting the spotlight on a small garden harvest to make a sensuous pudding, Nigel's clever tricks and inspired ideas show that you can often make bountiful feasts with apparently few ingredients.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The Bargain Hunt team pay a visit to the Royal Cornwall Showground. Anita Manning presents, and lending a hand to the teams are Phil Serrell and Tim Weeks. The teams race around the fair hoping to pick up three bargains, which they then take to auction. Meanwhile, surf's up for Anita as she pays a visit to Fistral Beach in Newquay to meet a surfing legend.

programme.title: The Password Is Courage
programme.desc: World War II drama based on an account of Sergeant Major Charles Coward, who was captured at Dunkirk in 1940 and dedicated his time in captivity to acts of sabotage and escape.

programme.title: The Wonder of Animals
programme.desc: Chris Packham explores the anatomy and physiology of the largest land animal on the planet - the elephant. Their size seems ill-suited to surviving the most arid regions of Africa, but their inner workings allow them to defy the extreme heat of the desert and find food and water in seemingly barren landscapes, while their extraordinary memory enables them to repel predators. Chris reveals how hairs on the skin help keep elephants cool, how sensors in their feet may be able to guide them towards rain and how a unique pouch in their mouths stores water. Recent research has even discovered that elephants can distinguish between the voices of human friend and foe.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This time, Flog It! comes from the RAF Museum in Cosford, Shropshire. Antiques experts Adam Partridge and Claire Rawle are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Claire gets sentimental over a music box and Adam discovers a silver cigarette case from Russia. Paul Martin falls for an iconic bike and visits the nearby historic Ironbridge to investigate the start of the industrial revolution.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Autumn brings challenges and rewards for farmers across Scotland. In Inverkip, Rachel and Camy are one year into building their own farm, taking on a tenancy at Dunrod Farm and a big bank loan with the dream of one day owning 5,000 sheep. But a trip to market means higher prices scupper their best intentions. In Maybole in South Ayrshire, the Barclay family are getting to grips with their new business venture – buying store lambs to fatten up for the butcher. After John’s father died suddenly last year, he’s trying to make their fourth generation farm work for them. A half-term break means a leisurely family day out… to the sheep auction. And in Moray, Nikki, Ollie and their children team up to process a bumper harvest of apples into juice for the whole year. Later, they find out if one of their favourite buffalo is pregnant.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 5 highlights from the second Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve takes on four entirely new adventures to some of the remotest parts of the planet in search of precious natural wonders. In the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Steve teams up with one of the world’s best free climbers, Leo Houlding, and former Royal Marine Aldo Kane. Together, they scale the highest peak in the ancient Dedan kingdom to unearth the secrets of this 2,500-year-old civilisation. In Gabon, Steve heads deep into the jungle to find a very special group of gorillas who have learned to trust humans – but who no-one has seen for nearly a year. In Mexico, Steve travels to the Sea of Cortez – known as the world’s aquarium – on a mission to free dive with mobula rays. Although they are protected by law, this incredibly rare marine species is under threat of extinction. In Kamchatka, Steve sets out to explore the Russian tundra in autumn, when brown bears are feasting on salmon. He witnesses a pristine, untouched wilderness where wildlife is unaffected by humans – a glimpse of the world as it should be.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes queen of country pop Shania Twain, global star Sam Smith, poet and songwriter Arlo Parks, Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine and Geordie jazz band Knats.

programme.title: TRNSMT
programme.desc: Shereen Cutkelvin presents highlights of the final day of TRNSMT from Glasgow Green, featuring CMAT, Skye Newman, Jacon Alon, Amy MacDonald, Perrie, Caity Baiser, Skye Newman and Lewis Capaldi.

programme.desc: Autumn brings challenges and rewards for farmers across Scotland. In Inverkip, Rachel and Camy are one year into building their own farm, taking on a tenancy at Dunrod Farm and a big bank loan with the dream of one day owning 5,000 sheep. But a trip to market means higher prices scupper their best intentions. In Maybole in South Ayrshire, the Barclay family are getting to grips with their new business venture – buying store lambs to fatten up for the butcher. After John’s father died suddenly last year, he’s trying to make their fourth generation farm work for them. A half-term break means a leisurely family day out… to the sheep auction. And in Moray, Nikki, Ollie and their children team up to process a bumper harvest of apples into juice for the whole year. Later, they find out if one of their favourite buffalo is pregnant.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 5 highlights from the second Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve takes on four entirely new adventures to some of the remotest parts of the planet in search of precious natural wonders. In the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Steve teams up with one of the world’s best free climbers, Leo Houlding, and former Royal Marine Aldo Kane. Together, they scale the highest peak in the ancient Dedan kingdom to unearth the secrets of this 2,500-year-old civilisation. In Gabon, Steve heads deep into the jungle to find a very special group of gorillas who have learned to trust humans – but who no-one has seen for nearly a year. In Mexico, Steve travels to the Sea of Cortez – known as the world’s aquarium – on a mission to free dive with mobula rays. Although they are protected by law, this incredibly rare marine species is under threat of extinction. In Kamchatka, Steve sets out to explore the Russian tundra in autumn, when brown bears are feasting on salmon. He witnesses a pristine, untouched wilderness where wildlife is unaffected by humans – a glimpse of the world as it should be.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: After 18 months behind bars, Sean returns to his community in Cambuslang, where he struggles to manage his ADHD, battles with addiction and faces a court case for armed robbery. Self-styled vigilante Frankie lives by his own brutal code of 'jail justice', which sees him attacking sex offenders, while violent offender and drug user Owen attempts to rebuild his life on the outside, until his violent past catches up with him.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools welcomes queen of country pop Shania Twain, global star Sam Smith, poet and songwriter Arlo Parks, Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine and Geordie jazz band Knats.

programme.title: TRNSMT
programme.desc: Shereen Cutkelvin presents highlights of the final day of TRNSMT from Glasgow Green, featuring CMAT, Skye Newman, Jacon Alon, Amy MacDonald, Perrie, Caity Baiser, Skye Newman and Lewis Capaldi.

programme.title: Death Valley
programme.desc: Whilst running a rehabilitation course for a group of rule-breaking police officers, Janie locks down CID when an attendee is found dead and brings John in to solve the case.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Zoe Ball follows in her ancestors’ footsteps in a journey that takes her from Scotland to Cornwall as she uncovers stories of resilience and the importance of family over place.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Vick Hope are in the Cotswolds, exploring one of Britain’s most iconic rural landscapes. While its rolling countryside, historic villages and farming heritage attract visitors from far and wide, protecting what makes the region special is an ongoing challenge. John meets the people helping to support nature and sustainable farming, while Vick discovers the skills and craftsmanship preserving the distinctive character of the Cotswolds. Meanwhile, Adam Henson gets hands-on with some of the region’s rare breeds and the efforts to secure their future.

programme.title: Capability Brown's Unfinished Garden
programme.desc: Capability Brown is known as the founder of landscape design. In the 1700s, he created some of the most magnificent landscapes in England. He travelled the length and breadth of the country, improving more than 200 of the greatest estates in the land for some of the most influential people of the 18th century. But there is one plan that never got off the drawing board. The only land Capability ever owned was in Fenstanton, Cambridgeshire, but he died before he could carry out any plans for his own garden. Today, it is a piece of flat land bisected by the A14 dual carriageway. Landscape designer and Gardeners' Question Time regular Bunny Guinness travels across England to some of Capability's finest landscapes - Blenheim, Burghley, Milton Abbey and Castle Ashby - to understand what he might have created. Rediscovering plans and letters, and using the latest technology, Capability Brown's unfinished garden is brought to life.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Beechgrove Garden is full of information for gardeners across the country who have to cope with the colder climates of the UK. Beechgrove has had some cold nights even recently, but now it looks like it’s safe to plant out those tender varieties, so Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham are finally putting in the ground varieties that wouldn't survive a frost. In a warmer environment, Lizzie is checking on her tomatoes, and this year she is comparing hybrid and heritage varieties, with both needing some attention right now to maximise their productivity. Brian is in the Accessible Garden looking at recent changes that will make the plot easier to move around and work in for anyone with mobility problems. There is also a trip to Leven to catch up with Calum in his allotment, and there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads to Montrose beach to measure the increasing rate of coastal erosion. Rosie is near Edinburgh meeting the farming brothers who regenerated their business into a top foodie destination. Shahbaz is in St Andrews finding out about the artists who accurately captured changes in our coastline before cameras were invented. Leanna visits Huntly to find out why it’s the perfect location for swifts. And as the annual clip gets underway, Cammy gives apprentice Anne a masterclass in the art of shearing.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt shares a delicious tasting menu from Saturday Kitchen chefs. Maria Elia serves up pulled duck burgers with an apple, peach and ouzo slaw and duck fat popcorn. Tony Singh rustles up langoustine en papillote with a honey, lime and ginger dressing, blanched asparagus and Jersey Royals on the side. To celebrate Britain’s love of a picnic, Matt has three variants on sausage rolls, from simple herbs to Mexican spices. Mandy Yin brings her Malaysian chicken curry and flaky flatbreads, while Julius Roberts cooks his courgette cavatelli. Olly Smith touts the virtues of chardonnay, and Paloma Faith tucks into either her food heaven, Spanish fish stew, or her food hell, beetroot pithivier. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes fishing for bass in Jersey, and the Hairy Bikers explore the fragrant benefits of bergamot.

programme.title: Mary Berry - Cook and Share
programme.desc: Mary bowls the England players over at Edgbaston with her cricket tea, steps onto the crease for a quick coaching session and shares more of her mouthwatering recipes.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Former Mr Gay Wales Paul Davies calls on Andi’s help to make Merthyr Tydfil’s first ever Pride a roaring success. While Prides have been popping up in the Welsh Valleys in recent years, this is set to be their biggest yet, but first there are two problems Andi needs to solve – food and transport. Andi sets about creating a true Valleys Pride flamboyant feast that uses local produce and draws on tradition while also celebrating difference. Then, in a bid to bring as many revellers as possible to this historic event, she hires a bus and tries to fill it with as many locals as possible, while also delving into the historic bond between miners and the gay and lesbian community, which dates back to the 1980s. With the Welsh weather threatening to make the whole event a washout, can Andi still bring the joy she’s promised Paul and make Merthyr’s inaugural Pride truly momentous?

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater raids his cupboards, fridge and vegetable patch to create a week's worth of delicious meals. In this edition, he demonstrates how to make our ingredients go just that little bit further. Whether it's adding grated beetroot to make a tasty meatball supper feed the masses, or putting the spotlight on a small garden harvest to make a sensuous pudding, Nigel's clever tricks and inspired ideas show that you can often make bountiful feasts with apparently few ingredients.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The Bargain Hunt team pay a visit to the Royal Cornwall Showground. Anita Manning presents, and lending a hand to the teams are Phil Serrell and Tim Weeks. The teams race around the fair hoping to pick up three bargains, which they then take to auction. Meanwhile, surf's up for Anita as she pays a visit to Fistral Beach in Newquay to meet a surfing legend.

programme.title: The Password Is Courage
programme.desc: World War II drama based on an account of Sergeant Major Charles Coward, who was captured at Dunkirk in 1940 and dedicated his time in captivity to acts of sabotage and escape.

programme.title: The Wonder of Animals
programme.desc: Chris Packham explores the anatomy and physiology of the largest land animal on the planet - the elephant. Their size seems ill-suited to surviving the most arid regions of Africa, but their inner workings allow them to defy the extreme heat of the desert and find food and water in seemingly barren landscapes, while their extraordinary memory enables them to repel predators. Chris reveals how hairs on the skin help keep elephants cool, how sensors in their feet may be able to guide them towards rain and how a unique pouch in their mouths stores water. Recent research has even discovered that elephants can distinguish between the voices of human friend and foe.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This time, Flog It! comes from the RAF Museum in Cosford, Shropshire. Antiques experts Adam Partridge and Claire Rawle are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Claire gets sentimental over a music box and Adam discovers a silver cigarette case from Russia. Paul Martin falls for an iconic bike and visits the nearby historic Ironbridge to investigate the start of the industrial revolution.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: The Game - The Story of Hurling
programme.desc: This episode explores the hunt for perfection within hurling. We see teams learning to win, with Galway’s breakthrough in the 1980s giving way to Ger Loughnane’s winning Clare side in the 1990s and Kilkenny’s fine-tuning of the pressure game in the 2000s. Tactics and fitness take on entirely new dimensions, and the rise of sports science elevates the standards expected of hurling giants. There is also a look at the women’s game and the battles camogie has had to fight to be recognised in its own right. As hurling has made its way through the early 2000s and the dawn of social media, what has that meant for the sport and the men and women who play it? For all the modern advancements in science and training, what lies at the heart of the game hasn’t changed at all – it’s still the magic of pure skill and the aura surrounding the heroes of the sport that draw the crowds in.

Their size seems ill-suited to surviving the most arid regions of Africa, but their inner workings allow them to defy the extreme heat of the desert and find food and water in seemingly barren landscapes, while their extraordinary memory enables them to repel predators. Chris reveals how hairs on the skin help keep elephants cool, how sensors in their feet may be able to guide them towards rain and how a unique pouch in their mouths stores water. Recent research has even discovered that elephants can distinguish between the voices of human friend and foe.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This time, Flog It! comes from the RAF Museum in Cosford, Shropshire. Antiques experts Adam Partridge and Claire Rawle are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Claire gets sentimental over a music box and Adam discovers a silver cigarette case from Russia. Paul Martin falls for an iconic bike and visits the nearby historic Ironbridge to investigate the start of the industrial revolution.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: Hidden behind two famous gardens lie the legacies of two extraordinary designers: garden designer Gertrude Jekyll at Munstead Wood, one of the National Trust's newest properties, and flamboyant set designer Oliver Messel at Nymans, which overlooks the Sussex Weald. Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Autumn brings challenges and rewards for farmers across Scotland. In Inverkip, Rachel and Camy are one year into building their own farm, taking on a tenancy at Dunrod Farm and a big bank loan with the dream of one day owning 5,000 sheep. But a trip to market means higher prices scupper their best intentions. In Maybole in South Ayrshire, the Barclay family are getting to grips with their new business venture – buying store lambs to fatten up for the butcher. After John’s father died suddenly last year, he’s trying to make their fourth generation farm work for them. A half-term break means a leisurely family day out… to the sheep auction. And in Moray, Nikki, Ollie and their children team up to process a bumper harvest of apples into juice for the whole year. Later, they find out if one of their favourite buffalo is pregnant.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 5 highlights from the second Test match between England and New Zealand.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve takes on four entirely new adventures to some of the remotest parts of the planet in search of precious natural wonders. In the desert kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Steve teams up with one of the world’s best free climbers, Leo Houlding, and former Royal Marine Aldo Kane. Together, they scale the highest peak in the ancient Dedan kingdom to unearth the secrets of this 2,500-year-old civilisation. In Gabon, Steve heads deep into the jungle to find a very special group of gorillas who have learned to trust humans – but who no-one has seen for nearly a year. In Mexico, Steve travels to the Sea of Cortez – known as the world’s aquarium – on a mission to free dive with mobula rays. Although they are protected by law, this incredibly rare marine species is under threat of extinction. In Kamchatka, Steve sets out to explore the Russian tundra in autumn, when brown bears are feasting on salmon. He witnesses a pristine, untouched wilderness where wildlife is unaffected by humans – a glimpse of the world as it should be.

programme.desc: Gareth Russell reveals the story of King James VI and I, his fondness for male favourites and a scandalous murder trial that threatened to blow his monarchy apart.

programme.desc: Whilst running a rehabilitation course for a group of rule-breaking police officers, Janie locks down CID when an attendee is found dead and brings John in to solve the case.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Zoe Ball follows in her ancestors’ footsteps in a journey that takes her from Scotland to Cornwall as she uncovers stories of resilience and the importance of family over place.

programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Vick Hope are in the Cotswolds, exploring one of Britain’s most iconic rural landscapes. While its rolling countryside, historic villages and farming heritage attract visitors from far and wide, protecting what makes the region special is an ongoing challenge. John meets the people helping to support nature and sustainable farming, while Vick discovers the skills and craftsmanship preserving the distinctive character of the Cotswolds. Meanwhile, Adam Henson gets hands-on with some of the region’s rare breeds and the efforts to secure their future.

programme.title: Capability Brown's Unfinished Garden
programme.desc: Capability Brown is known as the founder of landscape design. In the 1700s, he created some of the most magnificent landscapes in England. He travelled the length and breadth of the country, improving more than 200 of the greatest estates in the land for some of the most influential people of the 18th century. But there is one plan that never got off the drawing board. The only land Capability ever owned was in Fenstanton, Cambridgeshire, but he died before he could carry out any plans for his own garden. Today, it is a piece of flat land bisected by the A14 dual carriageway. Landscape designer and Gardeners' Question Time regular Bunny Guinness travels across England to some of Capability's finest landscapes - Blenheim, Burghley, Milton Abbey and Castle Ashby - to understand what he might have created. Rediscovering plans and letters, and using the latest technology, Capability Brown's unfinished garden is brought to life.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Beechgrove Garden is full of information for gardeners across the country who have to cope with the colder climates of the UK. Beechgrove has had some cold nights even recently, but now it looks like it’s safe to plant out those tender varieties, so Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham are finally putting in the ground varieties that wouldn't survive a frost. In a warmer environment, Lizzie is checking on her tomatoes, and this year she is comparing hybrid and heritage varieties, with both needing some attention right now to maximise their productivity. Brian is in the Accessible Garden looking at recent changes that will make the plot easier to move around and work in for anyone with mobility problems. There is also a trip to Leven to catch up with Calum in his allotment, and there are all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie heads to Montrose beach to measure the increasing rate of coastal erosion. Rosie is near Edinburgh meeting the farming brothers who regenerated their business into a top foodie destination. Shahbaz is in St Andrews finding out about the artists who accurately captured changes in our coastline before cameras were invented. Leanna visits Huntly to find out why it’s the perfect location for swifts. And as the annual clip gets underway, Cammy gives apprentice Anne a masterclass in the art of shearing.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt shares a delicious tasting menu from Saturday Kitchen chefs. Maria Elia serves up pulled duck burgers with an apple, peach and ouzo slaw and duck fat popcorn. Tony Singh rustles up langoustine en papillote with a honey, lime and ginger dressing, blanched asparagus and Jersey Royals on the side. To celebrate Britain’s love of a picnic, Matt has three variants on sausage rolls, from simple herbs to Mexican spices. Mandy Yin brings her Malaysian chicken curry and flaky flatbreads, while Julius Roberts cooks his courgette cavatelli. Olly Smith touts the virtues of chardonnay, and Paloma Faith tucks into either her food heaven, Spanish fish stew, or her food hell, beetroot pithivier. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes fishing for bass in Jersey, and the Hairy Bikers explore the fragrant benefits of bergamot.

programme.title: Mary Berry - Cook and Share
programme.desc: Mary bowls the England players over at Edgbaston with her cricket tea, steps onto the crease for a quick coaching session and shares more of her mouthwatering recipes.

programme.title: Andi Oliver’s Fabulous Feasts
programme.desc: Former Mr Gay Wales Paul Davies calls on Andi’s help to make Merthyr Tydfil’s first ever Pride a roaring success. While Prides have been popping up in the Welsh Valleys in recent years, this is set to be their biggest yet, but first there are two problems Andi needs to solve – food and transport. Andi sets about creating a true Valleys Pride flamboyant feast that uses local produce and draws on tradition while also celebrating difference. Then, in a bid to bring as many revellers as possible to this historic event, she hires a bus and tries to fill it with as many locals as possible, while also delving into the historic bond between miners and the gay and lesbian community, which dates back to the 1980s. With the Welsh weather threatening to make the whole event a washout, can Andi still bring the joy she’s promised Paul and make Merthyr’s inaugural Pride truly momentous?

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater raids his cupboards, fridge and vegetable patch to create a week's worth of delicious meals. In this edition, he demonstrates how to make our ingredients go just that little bit further. Whether it's adding grated beetroot to make a tasty meatball supper feed the masses, or putting the spotlight on a small garden harvest to make a sensuous pudding, Nigel's clever tricks and inspired ideas show that you can often make bountiful feasts with apparently few ingredients.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The Bargain Hunt team pay a visit to the Royal Cornwall Showground. Anita Manning presents, and lending a hand to the teams are Phil Serrell and Tim Weeks. The teams race around the fair hoping to pick up three bargains, which they then take to auction. Meanwhile, surf's up for Anita as she pays a visit to Fistral Beach in Newquay to meet a surfing legend.

programme.desc: Nick and Norman are going for a neighbourhood stroll when Nick discovers a stone in his shoe. How did it get there? The stone makes Nick do a funny dance, and the Popcasters help to write a song to go with his shaky leg.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Zigzag hasn’t had a poo in two days and doesn’t want to go on the scavenger hunt with her friends. Vida sets up a scavenger hunt just for her in the clinic, which is full of clues to help her go.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Pearl is sure Mara has Flailing Tail, but when purple spots appear on other patients, Zog and Gadabout suspect there is something afoot. Will Pearl listen to them?

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: At a party, Bingo is desperate to show off her handstand skills.

programme.desc: Animation. The Ribbon Sisters invite Sarah and Duck to their favourite seasonal event in the park.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Everybody in the school has to make a picture of their house for open day. Charlie, Marv, Lola and Lotta decide to make their pictures round at Charlie and Lola's. Lotta, who prides herself on being really good at drawing houses, suddenly can't draw anymore. The others find a way of inspiring Lotta and soon there's absolutely no stopping her.

programme.title: Moon and Me

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa discover a dandelion clock and have fun blowing the seeds. At Play Time, they choose another fuzzy flower to play with and bounce on a cloud whilst batting the flower about. The Yummies show MeMo and BaBa how to plant dandelion seeds, and MeMo and BaBa marvel at how a seed can become a beautiful flower. They travel across the Lullaby Lake, making their way to the Bay of Books.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Pinky Ponk gets stuck in a tree and tips up. Everybody slides up one end. They rock back and forth and tip the Pinky Ponk the other way. They slide up to the other end. Vet James is concerned about British Shorthair cat Nico as he has a limp in his hind legs, Fern meets Cocker Spaniel Nya as she enters the surgery for a scan on a potentially cancerous lump, vet Amy is in theatre and performing an operation on Border Terrier Dobby to remove an undescended testicle, nervous Cockapoo Jobo has to undergo an operation to have a lump removed from his ear by vet Andy, and we head outside the practice to Bristol's Guide Dog Centre to see puppies in training.

programme.title: From Russia with Love
programme.desc: The second entry in the James Bond spy film franchise and also the second movie to star Sean Connery as the fictional MI6 agent. 007 is on the search for a Russian decoding machine known as Lektor and needs to find this machine before the evil SPECTRE organisation discovers it. While being romantically linked with Russian Tatiana Romanova, James sneaks his way around Istanbul as SPECTRE agents - including the overpowering Donald 'Red' Grant and ex-KGB agent Rosa Klebb - try to pick him off.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined by old friend Raymond Blanc as he cooks a chocolate mousse - he calls it 'Maman Blanc' as it's a recipe that came from his mother. It's also a cheesecake day for Prue as she makes a Basque burnt cheesecake and a no-bake lemon and ginger cheesecake. Prue's food hero this time is Bold Beans and a farmer who produces some of the peas for the company - Prue and John then use some of those peas to make Indian pancakes with a carlin pea saag and paneer, and John is very happy that Prue has saved him some cheesecake and some of Raymond's chocolate mousse! While John heads to Tewkesbury to meet a woman who has revived an old tradition for making mustard balls, Prue has hacks for a mouthwatering burger sauce and a quick and healthy lunch using tinned sardines.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Crime drama series. The annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival draws in big audiences as several musicians anxiously compete for the coveted Falconer Bursary Award - shockwaves rocket though it when Jacob Wheeler is awarded the prize instead of the supremely talented Zac Sowande, but shock soon turns to horror when Jacob is found murdered strangled by violin string. Barnaby's initial investigations begin by focusing on Jacob's fellow musicians and their charismatic maestro Michael Falconer, who is using the festival to debut his Ninth Symphony while simultaneously belittling his own musician son Dan - when Barnaby realises that Jacob's Stradivarius is missing and that Jacob might not have been the completely dedicated musician his sister Natalie claims him to be, his subsequent investigations lead them deep into a world that is haunted by a potentially deadly curse.

programme.title: The Essex Millionaire Murders
programme.desc: The concluding part of a two-part documentary series. Detectives raid Luke D'Wit's home and seize a huge stash of prescription drugs - including fentanyl and antihistamine - that are both found in the Baxters' postmortem as police press Luke to explain his relationship to Carol Baxter's mysterious American physician Dr Andrea Bowden. Luke has been mixing 'medicinal' drinks for Carol on Dr Bowden's instructions, but detectives can find no trace of her existence - meanwhile, Ellena Baxter is completely cleared of her parents' murders and agrees to be interviewed as a witness for the police. As Ellena slowly realises that Luke has been a cuckoo in the family nest, detectives spend months combing through D'Wit's multiple digital devices to piece together the scale of his deception and cruelty.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. Raheel Ahmad looked the perfect match for TikTok photographer Sania Khan on paper - he came from a good family and wanted to be a doctor, but Raheel couldn't pass his medical exams once the couple had gotten married and then tried to hurl himself and her from the window of their 28th-storey Chicago apartment just months after their huge wedding. Hospitalised with mental problems, Raheel admitted that he had lied about his age and had been unfaithful - Sania then went public on TikTok with her agonies over whether to stick by her man or request a divorce. Her honesty and growing self-reliance resonated with abused women around the world and sent shockwaves through the South Asian community in America - the couple separated, but Raheel started to plot his revenge as Sania's posts went viral.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: The Essex Millionaire Murders
programme.desc: The concluding part of a two-part documentary series. Detectives raid Luke D'Wit's home and seize a huge stash of prescription drugs - including fentanyl and antihistamine - that are both found in the Baxters' postmortem as police press Luke to explain his relationship to Carol Baxter's mysterious American physician Dr Andrea Bowden. Luke has been mixing 'medicinal' drinks for Carol on Dr Bowden's instructions, but detectives can find no trace of her existence - meanwhile, Ellena Baxter is completely cleared of her parents' murders and agrees to be interviewed as a witness for the police. As Ellena slowly realises that Luke has been a cuckoo in the family nest, detectives spend months combing through D'Wit's multiple digital devices to piece together the scale of his deception and cruelty.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. Raheel Ahmad looked the perfect match for TikTok photographer Sania Khan on paper - he came from a good family and wanted to be a doctor, but Raheel couldn't pass his medical exams once the couple had gotten married and then tried to hurl himself and her from the window of their 28th-storey Chicago apartment just months after their huge wedding. Hospitalised with mental problems, Raheel admitted that he had lied about his age and had been unfaithful - Sania then went public on TikTok with her agonies over whether to stick by her man or request a divorce. Her honesty and growing self-reliance resonated with abused women around the world and sent shockwaves through the South Asian community in America - the couple separated, but Raheel started to plot his revenge as Sania's posts went viral.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined by old friend Raymond Blanc as he cooks a chocolate mousse - he calls it 'Maman Blanc' as it's a recipe that came from his mother. It's also a cheesecake day for Prue as she makes a Basque burnt cheesecake and a no-bake lemon and ginger cheesecake. Prue's food hero this time is Bold Beans and a farmer who produces some of the peas for the company - Prue and John then use some of those peas to make Indian pancakes with a carlin pea saag and paneer, and John is very happy that Prue has saved him some cheesecake and some of Raymond's chocolate mousse! While John heads to Tewkesbury to meet a woman who has revived an old tradition for making mustard balls, Prue has hacks for a mouthwatering burger sauce and a quick and healthy lunch using tinned sardines.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined by old friend Raymond Blanc as he cooks a chocolate mousse - he calls it 'Maman Blanc' as it's a recipe that came from his mother. It's also a cheesecake day for Prue as she makes a Basque burnt cheesecake and a no-bake lemon and ginger cheesecake. Prue's food hero this time is Bold Beans and a farmer who produces some of the peas for the company - Prue and John then use some of those peas to make Indian pancakes with a carlin pea saag and paneer, and John is very happy that Prue has saved him some cheesecake and some of Raymond's chocolate mousse! While John heads to Tewkesbury to meet a woman who has revived an old tradition for making mustard balls, Prue has hacks for a mouthwatering burger sauce and a quick and healthy lunch using tinned sardines.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Crime drama series. The annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival draws in big audiences as several musicians anxiously compete for the coveted Falconer Bursary Award - shockwaves rocket though it when Jacob Wheeler is awarded the prize instead of the supremely talented Zac Sowande, but shock soon turns to horror when Jacob is found murdered strangled by violin string. Barnaby's initial investigations begin by focusing on Jacob's fellow musicians and their charismatic maestro Michael Falconer, who is using the festival to debut his Ninth Symphony while simultaneously belittling his own musician son Dan - when Barnaby realises that Jacob's Stradivarius is missing and that Jacob might not have been the completely dedicated musician his sister Natalie claims him to be, his subsequent investigations lead them deep into a world that is haunted by a potentially deadly curse.

programme.title: The Essex Millionaire Murders
programme.desc: The concluding part of a two-part documentary series. Detectives raid Luke D'Wit's home and seize a huge stash of prescription drugs - including fentanyl and antihistamine - that are both found in the Baxters' postmortem as police press Luke to explain his relationship to Carol Baxter's mysterious American physician Dr Andrea Bowden. Luke has been mixing 'medicinal' drinks for Carol on Dr Bowden's instructions, but detectives can find no trace of her existence - meanwhile, Ellena Baxter is completely cleared of her parents' murders and agrees to be interviewed as a witness for the police. As Ellena slowly realises that Luke has been a cuckoo in the family nest, detectives spend months combing through D'Wit's multiple digital devices to piece together the scale of his deception and cruelty.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. Raheel Ahmad looked the perfect match for TikTok photographer Sania Khan on paper - he came from a good family and wanted to be a doctor, but Raheel couldn't pass his medical exams once the couple had gotten married and then tried to hurl himself and her from the window of their 28th-storey Chicago apartment just months after their huge wedding. Hospitalised with mental problems, Raheel admitted that he had lied about his age and had been unfaithful - Sania then went public on TikTok with her agonies over whether to stick by her man or request a divorce. Her honesty and growing self-reliance resonated with abused women around the world and sent shockwaves through the South Asian community in America - the couple separated, but Raheel started to plot his revenge as Sania's posts went viral.

programme.title: Syd
programme.desc: Syd is the inspirational story of a man who never backed down from a challenge. As a cricketer, David 'Syd' Lawrence was a fearsome fast bowler, who reached the top of the game to become the first British-born Black player to represent England. Although his career was cut short by an injury, described as one of the worst in sporting history, his achievements off the field have to be seen to be believed. In this film by Sabet Choudhury, Syd's family and friends including Phil Tufnell, Jonathan Agnew, Jack Russell and Sir Viv Richards recount a story that shows what can be achieved with a strong will and pure determination.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: In Donegal Town, Dermot's journey takes him further south along the Wild Atlantic Way, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its beautifully flecked fabric. Dressed fit for a fine meal, Dermot visits one of Ireland's most unexpected culinary hotspots: Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house. He meets Bangladeshi-born chef Rana, and together they cook railway curry using outstanding local Donegal lamb and potatoes - it's a heaven-made match of Asian flavours and quality Irish produce. For pudding, Dermot meets chef Brian McDermott, one of the biggest champions of Donegal's food scene. Together they bake a classic Irish apple pie, with Brian revealing why all the local rain creates richer grass, creamier milk and extra buttery pastry, making Donegal Town a dessert destination.

programme.title: Prue Leith's Cotswold Kitchen
programme.desc: Prue is joined by old friend Raymond Blanc as he cooks a chocolate mousse - he calls it 'Maman Blanc' as it's a recipe that came from his mother. It's also a cheesecake day for Prue as she makes a Basque burnt cheesecake and a no-bake lemon and ginger cheesecake. Prue's food hero this time is Bold Beans and a farmer who produces some of the peas for the company - Prue and John then use some of those peas to make Indian pancakes with a carlin pea saag and paneer, and John is very happy that Prue has saved him some cheesecake and some of Raymond's chocolate mousse! While John heads to Tewkesbury to meet a woman who has revived an old tradition for making mustard balls, Prue has hacks for a mouthwatering burger sauce and a quick and healthy lunch using tinned sardines.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Crime drama series. The annual Thassingham Classical Music Festival draws in big audiences as several musicians anxiously compete for the coveted Falconer Bursary Award - shockwaves rocket though it when Jacob Wheeler is awarded the prize instead of the supremely talented Zac Sowande, but shock soon turns to horror when Jacob is found murdered strangled by violin string. Barnaby's initial investigations begin by focusing on Jacob's fellow musicians and their charismatic maestro Michael Falconer, who is using the festival to debut his Ninth Symphony while simultaneously belittling his own musician son Dan - when Barnaby realises that Jacob's Stradivarius is missing and that Jacob might not have been the completely dedicated musician his sister Natalie claims him to be, his subsequent investigations lead them deep into a world that is haunted by a potentially deadly curse.
